findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates the live span and both synthetic row-skip paths, including merge-slot expansion; separate Markdown span clamping does not protect rendering.
findings.remediation:
Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Enforce explicit maximum live cell spans, row skips, aggregate table columns and merge slots before any allocation. Use checked sums and a cumulative layout resource budget, returning a typed refusal when exceeded.

findings.title: Processing renamed auxiliary XML bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained. Assigned discovery-0027 additionally confirms relationship-selected settings bytes reaching settings_dom/settings_dom_xml and unchecked DOM construction on cache miss; settings is now a supplied validated consumer, whereas earlier recommendations remain historical source limitations. Assigned discovery-0028 supplies already-validated linked-textbox and diagram consumers: relationship-ID media targets at src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428 and :17453-17464 are decoded and recursively parsed regardless of filename. The new source corroborates fontTable, theme, styles, numbering, settings, comments, notes and header/footer paths, and records that admission's content-type check covers the main part only. Assigned discovery-0031 additionally preserves strict normalization's extension-based pass-through: a relationship-selected fonts.bin remains unmodified before eager fontTable parsing. The raw unchecked parser's documented caller obligations are not themselves the finding.
findings.remediation: Apply active InputLimits at a centralized checked XML access/parse boundary for every semantic XML consumer regardless of filename, or resolve/classify and admit XML through actual content-type/relationship use. Cover theme, styles, numbering, converter comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; explicitly cover the now supplied validated settings_dom/settings_dom_xml cache-miss consumer, with earlier settings-only recommendations retained as historical source limitations. Preserve renamed-main checks, and enforce actual DOM construction depth or use iterative construction. Apply that same mandatory checked boundary to get_revisions and comparison notes parsing, including both footnotes and endnotes; propagate typed refusal under the active comparer InputLimits. Include pre_process_markup's relationship-selected notes at src/document_comparer.rs:4725-4750 and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions; valid arbitrary part names remain supported. Include linked-textbox and diagram relationship targets in the mandatory filename-independent checked XML boundary before parse_xdocument and in regression coverage. These are now supplied validated affected consumers from discovery-0028; earlier sources' proposed-only status remains historical. Cover revision_processor RevisionIds collection and process_part for all six selected auxiliary buckets (headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles), including public revision acceptance/rejection. Explicitly include the now-confirmed fontTable loader (src/convert/font_table.rs:66-78; src/convert/mod.rs:806) in the mandatory checked XML boundary; parsing must be bounded before any font root/entry inspection. Explicitly cover comparison defined_style_ids (src/document_comparer.rs:4684-4696), relationship-selected footnotes/endnotes (4724-4750) and chart preprocessing (4861-4878), all reached through admitted nonidentical comparison inputs (6555-6569,6607-6625). Apply the same mandatory XML boundary before edit initialization's existing_comment_ids scan, not only in the later checked CommentFamily loader; preserve the effective checks at inspect::parse_part_within and edit::load_stories. Enforce the same checked boundary before settings DOM cache population, and preserve valid bounded nonstandard auxiliary filenames.

findings.title: Reading or converting nested legacy DOC fields can monopolize the processing thread
findings.summary: An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.
findings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value
findings.summary:
A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies a static colspan=1000000000 framing of one billion 20-byte grid elements, about 20 GB of generated text before DOM construction; this is not a runtime measurement.
findings.remediation:
Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.
Additional retained remediation detail: Bound individual spans and aggregate columns before summation or iteration, use checked arithmetic, and impose a cumulative generated-WML byte/element budget shared across every HTML/MHT altChunk. Refuse excessive expansion with a typed input-limit error before allocation.

findings.title: WMF record-boundary failures amplify polygon work and retained text
findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies an additional static eight-byte TEXTOUT framing with a 65535-byte claimed string and overlapping following bytes. About 1 MiB can request multiple gigabytes of retained text; valid whole-file reads, nonblank text and nonzero mapping extents remain required. No out-of-bounds memory read is asserted.
findings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

findings.title: Aliased legacy DOC pieces expand small physical text into enormous logical stories
findings.summary:
Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies 65535 contiguous pieces of 65535 compressed characters sharing one 65535-byte physical range: 4294836225 logical CPs within u32 and about 786 KB of piece records. These are static counts.
findings.remediation:
Introduce configurable legacy physical-input, piece-count, cumulative logical-character, retained-metadata and expansion-work budgets. Check FIB ccp_text and checked cumulative piece lengths before materialization, charge every decoded character including repeated physical aliases, and return typed refusals through read/doc_to_markdown/doc_to_docx and CLI callers. Preserve legitimate fast-save aliases and split UTF-16 surrogate handling within budget. Replace full legacy parsing used only for diagnostic refusal hints with a cheap bounded probe, or apply the same logical/work budgets before that parser runs.
Additional retained remediation detail: Introduce a configurable legacy logical-character/output budget, check ccp_text and cumulative decoded piece work before materialization, and enforce it during decoding. Preserve valid reuse while returning a typed refusal for excessive expansion.

findings.title: Rendering an admitted DOCX can retain gigabytes of duplicate embedded fonts
findings.summary: Distinct font-table aliases may all reference one embedded font part. Rendering eagerly loads every alias, copies the full font and retains a separate buffer for each name, multiplying a small admitted package into gigabytes of memory even if its body never uses those fonts. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates distinct invented family names bypassing known-catalogue exclusions; valid Face::parse results and the later u16 face-index limit do not bound earlier alias copies.
findings.remediation:
Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.
Enforce face-count limits before decoding/retention and load only used faces where possible; cover all four style slots and different effective keys.

findings.title: Repeated relationship IDs trigger quadratic repair work
findings.summary: Opening a package repairs identical duplicate relationship IDs. For n distinct IDs each repeated identically, each repair linearly searches an increasingly long Vec, producing quadratic CPU work on shallow metadata that fits existing byte and attribute limits. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.
findings.remediation: Track already-reported duplicate IDs in a HashSet or alongside seen-map state, retaining a Vec only for deterministic reporting order. Optionally cap relationship-record/work totals before repair; test many distinct identical duplicate pairs while preserving deterministic repaired-ID order and conflicting-duplicate refusals. Apply an active relationship-record/work budget at metadata admission in addition to making duplicate membership near-linear.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.
findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

findings.title: Pull-request code runs on shared self-hosted infrastructure
findings.summary:
A lower-trust PR admitted to run can change a local action, build script, test or generator and execute it with self-hosted runner privileges. Four workflows share this missing isolation boundary; the local cache action documents private tokenless cache connectivity and reused checkout/disk. A permitted run also inherits the documented private Docker network and tokenless mbx-cache endpoint; cache poisoning, persistence and additional internal service access remain unverified deployment-dependent outcomes. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates permitted fork execution across all four workflows and the documented tokenless private Docker cache network/reused checkouts. contents:read, persist-credentials:false and normal client-side PR cache-read policy do not establish process/network isolation. Actual approvals, worker lifecycle and server authorization remain unverified.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates permitted fork execution in CI/docs/md-roundtrip/adoption and the documented private tokenless cache network, reused checkouts and persistent stores; actual approval, runner isolation and service authorization remain unverified.
findings.remediation:
Run lower-trust PR builds/tests/generators on GitHub-hosted or one-job disposable runners without trusted writable state or private infrastructure connectivity. Separate trusted main runners and enforce cache write authorization server-side. Apply consistently to ci, adoption, docs and md-roundtrip.
Additional retained remediation detail: Run untrusted PR jobs on GitHub-hosted or disposable isolated workers without trusted persistent stores/private services. Gate access to the shared self-hosted pool using trusted workflow logic outside PR control. Enforce cache read-only access at the service boundary when PRs need it.

findings.title: Ragged legacy DOC tables expand into an unbounded padded rectangle
findings.summary: A table with one wide row and many narrow rows contains relatively few cells, but legacy Markdown serialization emits the widest row's cell count for every row. Compact input can therefore generate gigabytes of output and exhaust importer memory. The same unbounded serialization is independently exposed through public to_markdown(LegacyDocument), in addition to DOC byte conversions. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 100000-cell row plus 100000 short/empty rows framing: about ten billion serialized cells before DOCX admission. No numeric colspan forgery or logical-piece alias is required.
findings.remediation: Before rectangularizing a table, use checked multiplication to enforce a generated-cell quota and enforce cumulative output-byte/work limits. Refuse over-budget tables with a typed error. Enforce a supported column ceiling and cover doc_to_markdown and doc_to_docx's Markdown intermediate; a bounded sparse representation is another option.

findings.title: Repeated compressed-image references can exhaust renderer memory
findings.summary: A DOCX can reference one highly compressible embedded image many times. Conversion independently decodes and retains an owned pixel buffer per reference, then clones buffers into page operations. Package byte limits and per-page pixel limits do not bound this aggregate decoded memory. The assigned source confirms image 0.25.10's default 512 MiB allocation limit applies separately to each decode. A 4096x4096 RGBA raster requires about 64 MiB per occurrence and a hundred references retain gigabytes; authored drawing/page extents do not cap intrinsic decoded storage. These are supplied static counts. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a static 1000-reference framing for one ordinary solid 2048x2048 PNG: about 11.7 GiB of retained RGB alone before page painting. Group-picture, VML-preview and picture-bullet paths also independently decode resources; destination MAX_PAGE_PIXELS and per-decode limits do not bound aggregate retention.
findings.remediation: Apply a conversion-wide decoded-pixel/byte budget before decoding or retaining media, cache decoded parts by source and transformation, and use shared immutable samples in layout/display operations. Count transformed and temporary buffers against the same budget. Apply the same sharing and aggregate accounting to group-picture, VML-preview and picture-bullet consumers, keyed by effective transformation; retain all earlier display-list/temporary-buffer accounting.

findings.title: Legacy DOC placeholder selection repeatedly rescans predictable document text
findings.summary: DOC-to-DOCX conversion unconditionally searches all authored text for sequential predictable placeholder candidates, with no bounded selection algorithm. A few megabytes containing consecutive jubarteemptyparagraph0 through jubarteemptyparagraph99999 force about100000 increasingly long searches, occupying conversion CPU.
findings.remediation: Skip placeholder selection when no empty paragraph requires it. Otherwise scan text once for occupied candidate suffixes or construct a delimiter using a bounded number of linear passes.

findings.title: Report text extraction quadratically groups baselines on tall pages
findings.summary: page_text searches the entire existing-baseline Vec for every text op, while document-controlled page height permits arbitrarily many distinct baselines on a single page. 100000 distinct one-character baselines cause about5billion key comparisons. A report-only request does not pass through MAX_PAGE_PIXELS destination allocation checks.
findings.remediation: Index baseline keys with a HashMap or BTreeMap while retaining first-seen output order; enforce aggregate text-operation/work limits independently of raster page-size limits.
